headline: SILVER CRATERS TO 6-MONTH LOW AT $43 — 'Very Limited Downside' From Here, Analyst Argues; $40 Zone Next Key Floor
snippet: Spot silver fell to its lowest level in over six months at approximately $42.96 on November 20 — a 30%+ decline from its 2026 year-to-date peak — as a strengthening US dollar and near-certain December Fed rate hike expectations combined to create unusually intense downward pressure on the metal. Despite the severity of the fall, at least one analyst argues downside from current levels is very limited, citing coin and bar demand picking up below $44 and the $40 zone as a structural support backed by physical buyers who consistently defended the level through the 2024-2025 trading range; the selloff has also pushed the gold-silver ratio to levels historically associated with silver being undervalued versus gold, a relative-value metric long-term precious metals investors use to assess positioning.

headline: LITHIUM AFRICA ML HITS NEW PEGMATITE 11km AWAY — 2.21% Li2O at Jackal Water; Springbok District Doubles in Footprint
snippet: Lithium Africa (TSX-V: LAF) reported the discovery of a new lithium-bearing pegmatite system at Jackal Water on November 19, located 11 kilometres southwest of the Norrabees cluster at its Springbok Project in South Africa's Northern Cape — found using the company's proprietary machine-learning geotargeting algorithm rather than conventional soil sampling. Initial drilling across eight holes intersected 11 to 56 metres of logged pegmatite downhole with the best assay returning 2.21% Li2O over 1.0 metre, while two rigs continue drilling with additional assays pending across the 1,675 km² property; the discovery effectively doubles the Springbok district footprint and adds a second high-priority drill area alongside Norrabees III — which returned lithium in all 12 holes two days prior — building a district-scale investment case at a low point in the global lithium market cycle.

headline: SCHIFF CALLS SILVER SELLOFF A 'GREAT BUYING OPPORTUNITY' — Steepest 2-Month Drop Flagged for PAAS, AG, HL Accumulation
snippet: Peter Schiff labelled November 20's precious metals selloff — in which silver suffered its steepest single-day percentage decline in over two months — a 'great buying opportunity,' arguing that the dollar-driven move reflects a temporary financial conditions shock rather than any fundamental shift in gold and silver's long-term bull market thesis. Schiff specifically flagged Pan American Silver (PAAS), First Majestic (AG), and Hecla Mining (HL), all down more than 3-4% in the session, as names where investors can accumulate positions at the most compressed valuations since mid-2025; his view is that coordinated futures selling is driving the disconnect between paper-market pricing and physical demand, which remains strong based on coin, bar, and commercial buying levels at current prices.

headline: NEM, OR ROYALTIES, TOREX — Simply Wall St Nov 2026 Gold Screen; Balance Sheet and AISC Rank Them Top for Selloff Entry
snippet: Simply Wall St's November 2026 gold stock screen highlights Newmont Mining (NYSE: NEM), Sandstorm Gold Royalties (TSX: OR), and Torex Gold Resources (TSX: TXG) as three names with the strongest combination of balance sheet health, all-in sustaining cost (AISC) efficiency, and geographic diversification for navigating the current correction. The methodology specifically screens for below-sector-average debt-to-equity, positive free cash flow at $3,400-$3,500 gold, and management track records of cost discipline — criteria that exclude the more leveraged mid-tiers experiencing the steepest drawdowns; for retail investors who want gold producer exposure without trying to pick the bottom in development-stage juniors, the analysis provides a risk-adjusted starting point for building a position list among seniors and royalty names rather than chasing the most beaten-down exploration stocks.

headline: TSX RETREATS AS METALS SLIDE AND AI DOUBTS GROW — Mining-Heavy Index Lags Global Peers; Sector Support Tested
snippet: Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index pulled back sharply as a simultaneous selloff in precious and base metals combined with renewed investor skepticism over AI-driven copper demand to push the index significantly below global peers in a session where European and US markets held flatter or recovered. The dual headwind has particular bite on the TSX because gold, silver, and copper producers collectively represent over 20% of the index's market capitalisation, meaning corrections in those commodities translate almost immediately into broad index-level underperformance; for retail investors evaluating TSX broad-market exposure versus sector-specific mining allocation, the index's metals sensitivity creates both a risk factor and an opportunity depending on conviction about how long the current correction in metals prices persists.

headline: COPPER BOUNCES AS AI SENTIMENT LIFTS AND CHINA SQUEEZES SUPPLY — Physical Market Tight Even as LME Futures Lag Recovery
snippet: Copper futures bounced off near-term lows as a brief recovery in AI-related technology stocks removed some of the demand pessimism that has pressured the metal in recent weeks, while supply data from China simultaneously reinforced the physical market's tightness — with SHFE copper inventories at their lowest levels in nearly three years and Yangshan import premiums holding near record levels despite the futures selloff. The disconnect between paper and physical copper is the key signal that experienced copper investors are tracking: futures are responding to AI demand uncertainty while China's physical market signals genuine supply constraints, a divergence that has historically preceded sharp futures recoveries once speculative positioning normalises and actual supply data reasserts itself.

headline: TSX MINING STOCKS SIGNAL NEW PRIORITIES — Capital Rotates to Copper, Uranium as Gold, Lithium Face Headwinds
snippet: An analysis of TSX mining stock performance patterns in November 2026 identifies a rotation in institutional capital flows, with copper producers and uranium developers attracting relative inflows while gold equities and lithium developers face continued outflows — a reallocation reflecting infrastructure and energy transition investment themes rather than a pure precious metals thesis. Names with copper or uranium exposure alongside gold assets are holding valuations better than pure-play precious metals, suggesting institutional investors are repositioning toward commodities most directly tied to electricity infrastructure buildout, independent of the gold price correction; for TSX-V retail investors deciding how to express current sector views, the rotation data provides context for position sizing across a diversified junior mining portfolio rather than concentrating entirely in gold explorers at this stage of the correction.

headline: NEWMONT -3%, FREEPORT -2% AS GOLD BREAKS KEY LEVEL NOV 18 — NEM P/E Compresses to 14x; GDX Hits One-Year Low
snippet: Spot gold dropped more than 2% on November 18 to a one-year low, pulling Newmont (NYSE: NEM) down approximately 3% and Freeport-McMoRan (NYSE: FCX) lower as broad selling pressure drove the GDX gold miners ETF to its lowest close in over a year. Despite the price pressure, Newmont's forward P/E has compressed to approximately 14x — below its five-year median — even as year-on-year 2026 earnings growth consensus runs at approximately 33% higher than 2025, creating a disconnect between operational performance and equity market sentiment; for retail investors considering large-cap gold exposure as a risk-adjusted proxy for a gold price recovery, the NEM/FCX valuation data provides benchmark levels for evaluating whether current prices represent a margin-of-safety entry or simply the front end of a continuing decline.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER TUMBLE TRIGGERS MINING RESET — P/NAV at Decade Lows for TSX Developers; Generational Entry Setup Forming
snippet: A Yahoo Finance analysis describes the ongoing gold and silver price correction — gold down approximately 16% from its 2026 all-time high and silver off roughly 30% — as a 'major reset' that has pushed gold mining stocks to price-to-NAV ratios not seen in roughly a decade, with some TSX-V developers below 0.5x NAV for the first time since 2015. The analysis frames the disconnect as a potential setup similar to 2016 and 2019, when previous similar dislocations between miner valuations and gold prices resolved with multi-year equity outperformance; it notes the current environment is unusual because miners are cheap relative to gold at the same time record margins and cash flows make the fundamental case stronger than in past cycles — a combination that has historically attracted generalist capital once the near-term rate and dollar headwinds resolve.

headline: SHAKEOUT OR CYCLE TOP? — Mining Stock Monkey Reviews 3 Historical Signals for Junior Miner Timing Decisions
snippet: Mining Stock Monkey's latest analysis frames the central question that every TSX-V exploration investor faces in November 2026: is this a mid-cycle shakeout — historically the best buying opportunity in a multi-year bull market — or the beginning of a multi-year bear cycle that will punish premature long entries? The piece draws on historical patterns from 2008, 2012, and 2018 to identify three specific indicators that have most reliably distinguished these two scenarios: the direction of central bank gold buying, the spread between physical and paper gold market premiums, and the behaviour of junior exploration stocks relative to senior producers on the initial bounce; it suggests a phased capital deployment approach for investors who want exposure without fully committing before direction becomes clear.
